$description: Tile Steps' design tokens, in the W3C Design Tokens format (2025.10): every colour (light values here, dark in tokens.dark.json) and every size. python -m design.tokens write puts them into web/src/tokens.css; check fails when that file is stale or a pair below misses its contrast. Never write a raw colour or size in the app: add a token here.

surface.$description: the page: warm paper, like a toy box lid

surface-2.$description: raised things on the page: cards, the step panel, dialogs

surface-3.$description: pressed and selected states; the shelf behind project cards

ink-1.$description: main text and icons; kid labels

ink-2.$description: secondary text: a card's subtitle, a setting's help

ink-3.$description: the quietest text the grown-ups side uses: a timestamp, a hint

line.$description: hairlines and card edges (decoration; never the only edge of a control)

accent.$description: the one brand colour, a sunny burnt orange: the primary button (Next, Build it), the selected age, the focus ring's base

accent-ink.$description: text and icons on the accent

accent-soft.$description: a tint of the accent behind a selected chip

focus.$description: the keyboard and switch-control focus ring

can-bg.$description: behind "You can build it!": always with the check shape, never colour alone

can-ink.$description: the words and check on can-bg

wait-bg.$description: behind "Need 2 more": always with the missing tiles drawn

stage.$description: behind the 3D model: warm light over the table

ground.$description: the wooden table the 3D model stands on

tile-red.$description: the red tile's colour (fills are drawn at 45% over the surface, with a pattern and a rim)

tile-red-rim.$description: the red tile's rim: the edge that gives the tile 3:1 against the page

tile-orange.$description: the orange tile's colour (fills are drawn at 45% over the surface, with a pattern and a rim)

tile-orange-rim.$description: the orange tile's rim: the edge that gives the tile 3:1 against the page

tile-yellow.$description: the yellow tile's colour (fills are drawn at 45% over the surface, with a pattern and a rim)

tile-yellow-rim.$description: the yellow tile's rim: the edge that gives the tile 3:1 against the page

tile-green.$description: the green tile's colour (fills are drawn at 45% over the surface, with a pattern and a rim)

tile-green-rim.$description: the green tile's rim: the edge that gives the tile 3:1 against the page

tile-blue.$description: the blue tile's colour (fills are drawn at 45% over the surface, with a pattern and a rim)

tile-blue-rim.$description: the blue tile's rim: the edge that gives the tile 3:1 against the page

tile-purple.$description: the purple tile's colour (fills are drawn at 45% over the surface, with a pattern and a rim)

tile-purple-rim.$description: the purple tile's rim: the edge that gives the tile 3:1 against the page

fs-kid-label-a.$description: kid words (labels, a step's text) for ages 3–5; about 4 mm lowercase at 5 to 7 (kids-app-design.md, section 3)

fs-kid-label-b.$description: kid words (labels, a step's text) for ages 6–8; about 4 mm lowercase at 5 to 7 (kids-app-design.md, section 3)

fs-kid-label-c.$description: kid words (labels, a step's text) for ages 9–10; about 4 mm lowercase at 5 to 7 (kids-app-design.md, section 3)

fs-kid-count-a.$description: the count on a tile chip (×4) for ages 3–5

fs-kid-count-b.$description: the count on a tile chip (×4) for ages 6–8

fs-kid-count-c.$description: the count on a tile chip (×4) for ages 9–10

target-kid-primary.$description: Next, Build it, Back to the shelf: the one big button, about 2.2 cm on an 11-inch iPad (NN/g)

target-kid-a.$description: every other kid control for ages 3–5

target-kid-b.$description: every other kid control for ages 6–8

target-kid-c.$description: every other kid control for ages 9–10

gap-kid.$description: the least space between two kid controls

gap-parent.$description: the least space between two grown-ups controls

hit-slop-kid.$description: how far a kid control's tap area reaches past its edge

edge-safe-kid.$description: no kid control within this of the screen's edge (plus the safe area)

r-tile.$description: close to a real tile's corner

rim.$description: the rim of a tile picture, and the border of a kid control

t-celebrate.$description: the end-of-build celebration, at most; skippable

turn-period.$description: one full slow turn of the 3D model (ages 9–10 only; never during a 3–5 step)

display.$description: titles: round and friendly, used sparingly

kid.$description: every word a child reads: single-storey a and g
